hypothesis: Does standard scalar-verifier GRPO improve planning, and does predicted-contract input change its effect relative to matched continued SFT?
sampling: temperature=1, top_p=1, top_k=0, dropout disabled; no truncated-distribution likelihood mismatch
reward: Gold-verifier faithful_success, including minimal change and N default preservation; predicted contract is input only
algorithm: Token-wise clipped old-policy surrogate plus k3 KL to frozen shared SFT reference, group population-standardized outcome advantages, equal completion-mean weighting; two actual updates per sampled batch
comparison: Same initial policy and 96 train tasks as matched SFT, 24 optimizer updates each; unequal rollout/token compute reported explicitly
budget: 2 arms x384 training samples +576 greedy eval calls; existing compiler cache reused with cost attribution; 30min training and20min evaluation per arm,110min outer cap
selection: Final fixed24-update checkpoint only; all failed or partial runs retained; no dev-based checkpoint selection
scope: Exploratory seed42 baseline on exposed dev panel; not a novel GRPO method or official TRL reproduction
